claims.reason: `hp` is only a binder of the theorem; the statement never mentions it, so deleting it leaves a statement that still elaborates. In Mathlib, `ordCompl[p] n` is notation for `n / ordProj[p] n`, and `ordProj[p] n` is `p ^ n.factorization p` (Defs.lean:330). `Nat.factorization_eq_zero_of_not_prime (n : ℕ) {p} (hp : ¬p.Prime) : n.factorization p = 0` exists (Defs.lean:129). Proof without `hp`: case on whether `p` is prime. If it is, the original proof goes through unchanged. If it is not, both factorizations are 0, so the right side becomes `gcd (m / p^0) (n / p^0) * p^(min 0 0) = gcd m n * 1 = gcd m n`, and `simp` closes the goal. This covers p = 0 and p = 1, since neither is prime. So the theorem is true and provable without `hp`, and `hm` and `hn` can stay as they are.
